title: 5. Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) – VERY HIGH PROBABILITY

blocks.content: The Central Administrative Tribunal was established in 1985 under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 to adjudicate disputes related to recruitment and service conditions of public servants.
In the L. Chandra Kumar (1997) judgment, the Supreme Court ruled that tribunal decisions are subject to judicial review by High Courts, restoring the power of constitutional courts.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) was created in 1985 under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985.
Its main function is to adjudicate disputes concerning the recruitment and service conditions of public servants.
The 1997 L. Chandra Kumar judgment subjected tribunal decisions to High Court judicial review.

CAT handles service conditions and recruitment disputes for public servants specifically.
